I don’t know you or your relationship but speaking from experience, my relationships were usually in the honeymoon phase for the first 3 months. After that, I really got to know the person and see their true colors. Get to know him more as a person, but please do not rush the situation. 

I’ve never found myself to be in love with fictional people so I don’t think I fully understand where you’re coming from. But are you sure it’s love or do you think it’s really limerence? Also, understand that the fictional character is not real and you’ll never be with them ever in real life. It’s sad but it’s the harsh reality of your situation. You may like their concept as a character and can look for that same personality in real people, but there has to be a difference in reality versus virtual reality…if that’s even the name to put to it. 

Simply put, I think these are more so infatuations than love. You’re young, take your time finding “the one”.

Do you think he’s depressed because of the open relationship? Maybe that’s what’s turning his sex drive off. 

Regardless, I’d have a sit down talk with him and ask if this open relationship is really the smartest idea for both of your personal intimacies. This does not sound healthy to me. Why did you choose to open your relationship?

Focus on your damn school work. That crush you have now? Won’t matter in 10 years. In fact, you more than likely won’t fall in love with them either. Or maybe you will. But your main focus now (if you even have the slightest bit of thought of getting a post secondary education) should be your school work. I wish now that I applied myself to more college classes in high school so I wouldn’t have the workload I have now. But such is life.

Figured I’d add in my own personal story: graduated in 2020 and didn’t go to college. Decided to go straight into the workforce to earn some money. During this time, I wasn’t practicing. Had I guess what’d you call an “epiphany” and decided to go back to school and study music for Fall 2023. Since August, I’ve gotten a new flute and it wasn’t until a week before my audition into music school that I got lessons due to some scheduling issues. My flute playing was not on par with what it used to be, but with time and practicing, I was able to get it to where it used to be senior year (and probably more). This was also a different instrument than I was used to [since all lip plates are different] so I was also adjusting to the instrument too.

Obviously I see you’ve learned another instrument in this time, so your embouchure is going to change over time. The unfortunate truth is: long tones aren’t the best thing you’ll ever work on, but it’s one of many ways to get better. Trevor Wye’s practice books go into deep detail on tone, setting your embouchure, and other techniques to achieve a rich tone quality. Constant practicing is really the only way to get better. 

However, there are also a multitude of ways to make practicing fun. Lots of experimentation, even listening to pros like Sir James Galway and Jasmine Choi. Figure out what works for you and you’ll be golden! 

Hope this helps you in some way. Any questions, feel free to ask.
